subject.title: contextPruning (mode: cache-ttl) never fires on OpenAI models: isCacheTtlEligibleProvider excludes OpenAI, so the idle-gap tool-result firebreak is dead for the highest-volume provider

question: Should OpenAI cache-TTL pruning be enabled by widening provider eligibility, by adding provider-agnostic or retention-aware pruning semantics, or left disabled until a broader cache policy is designed?
rationale: Current source proves the OpenAI no-op, but changing the shared eligibility gate affects upgrade behavior and retained OpenAI session context, so the permanent policy needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Retention-aware or provider-agnostic pruning
options.body: Use a pruning policy that does not assume Anthropic-style cache TTL semantics and require native OpenAI proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Approve native OpenAI eligibility
options.body: Accept that existing OpenAI `cache-ttl` configs become active under the current TTL semantics, with explicit compatibility notes and focused tests.

options.title: Defer OpenAI pruning
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers decide whether OpenAI prefix caching should be handled in a broader context-management redesign.

recommendation.title: Retention-aware or provider-agnostic pruning
recommendation.body: Use a pruning policy that does not assume Anthropic-style cache TTL semantics and require native OpenAI proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about OpenAI prompt-cache semantics, and Peter has the strongest adjacent history on prompt-caching docs and OpenAI runtime behavior in the inspected history.
